solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Further cuts a local's opposed to

definitions.note: a dialect word, as a local might say it, for against

indicators.note: cuts says the word a is removed from the synonym for further

parts.note: further, as in 'once more', means again

explanation.surface: Someone reads that further spending cuts are something a local person is against.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect form of against, heard in rural speech: 'I'm agin it'.

clue.text: 2/4A Group of 10s, leading one, finally winning — er … not as it turned out

indicators.note: the letters that turned out are rearranged, so this signals a shuffle of the preceding words
finally picks the closing letter of the word winning

explanation.surface: England's star squad, the leaders who were supposed to win at last, didn't, as events showed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it turned out' shuffles LEADING, ONE, G (last of winning), ER and NOT, sixteen letters in all. The phrase was the press's name for England's star footballers of the 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort of top-rated players, each a 'perfect ten', was hailed by the English press as a gilded era of talent.

clue.text: Back in front in Argentina's group

indicators.note: back says the little word in is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: RA is Argentina's international vehicle registration code
the van is the front of an army or procession

explanation.surface: A football fan is told someone has come back into the leading pack of Argentina's World Cup group.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, from the international car plates, is Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock band from Seattle fronted by Kurt Cobain is a musical group.

clue.text: Boiled egg tonight — husband declined to be enterprising

indicators.note: boiled, like eggs churned in water, says the letters are scrambled
declined, refused to take part, says the H leaves the word tonight

explanation.surface: A husband turned down a boiled egg for supper, choosing to be adventurous instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declined' removes H from TONIGHT, leaving TONIGT; 'Boiled' shuffles EGG with that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambitious and energetic, keen to seize opportunities: a synonym.

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted means raised, so the word goes upward and reads backwards

parts.note: half of a score of twenty is ten

explanation.surface: A teacher marks only half the score that a pupil earned on promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' does double duty: as twenty it makes half equal TEN, which 'when promoted' turns upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To find the back of the goal, scoring, as a footballer does.

clue.text: Reverse of swindle in Yorkshire city?

indicators.note: the reverse, meaning opposite, of the last part of the swindle word is swapped in for it

parts.note: a swindle is a rip-off

explanation.surface: A puzzled question asks whether a con trick was run backwards in some northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of OFF is ON, so RIP-OFF becomes RIP-ON. Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England.

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the two letters are read the other way

parts.note: RT is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon
to benefit is to avail, as in 'it availed him nothing'

explanation.surface: A political line: the Labour Party is right to make a fuss about state benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party; here it means toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Toil, hard work, or the pains of childbirth: a synonym.

indicators.note: short says the synonym for public loses its last letter

parts.note: something public is overt, open to view
a look is an appearance

explanation.surface: A celebrity regrets a brief public appearance, or a fan failed to see it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to notice or to pass over: a synonym.

definitions.meaning: the reply to 'is anything wrong?' saying everything is fine

explanation.surface: A worried question gets a reassuring no, then a cheerful yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase both answers 'is something wrong?' with 'fine' and means 'okay' as agreement.

indicators.note: parts means splits open, so the latin word for each is divided to take the other piece

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'
to lay is to arrange, as in laying a table

explanation.surface: A director assigns roles to every actor in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like theatre roles; here it is a verb meaning splits open.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor, musician or sportsman is someone who plays.

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the crossword's usual army unit
something gone is past

explanation.surface: Troops have left to get something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal or literary word for a meal or feast.

clue.text: Top hotel in slightly dodgy place

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
slightly dodgy suggests a small rearrangement, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A top hotel turns out to be in a rather shady location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slightly dodgy' makes PACLE: only two letters change places.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or highest point of something: a synonym.

clue.text: After spin, handle top fast bowler

indicators.note: after spin means the pieces are turned round, so they read backwards

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes that once the spinner is done, the captain should bring on his top quick bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, spin bowling and fast bowling are contrasting styles, so 'spin' leads one to expect a spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a pace bowler is one who relies on speed.

definitions.note: the blank stands for the name of England's Italian football manager at the 2010 World Cup

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A tabloid jeers at the England manager: capable? A failure, so goodbye, from Harry Redknapp, tipped to succeed him.
explanation.walkthrough: The blanks stand for the answer. 'Harry' signals shuffling the letters of ABLE, FLOP and CIAO.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank lines in the clue fill in the name of the Italian who managed England, 2008-2012.

clue.text: English plans miscarry, getting draw and what may follow (19 to 25?)

indicators.note: getting means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other
plans that miscarry go wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match

explanation.surface: English tactics go wrong, a drawn game results, and the dreaded shoot-out against Germany may follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miscarry' makes PENALS, opened before the S. A drawn knockout match is settled by a shoot-out; 19 and 25 hint at LOSING to THE GERMANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot kicks taken to settle a knockout football match that ends level.

clue.text: Walk further than border with pain in joints — not good

indicators.note: not says the letter for good is left out

parts.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints
a march is a border region, as in the Welsh Marches

explanation.surface: A sufferer limps along the boundary, aching joints making the walk feel endless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marches are the historic borderlands between England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone in marching, covering more ground on foot.

clue.text: Meeting run badly — man's not strictly organised

indicators.note: badly signals the words are to be jumbled

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A shambolic meeting was chaired by a man who is not very orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally free from military regimentation, so loose and not rigidly organised.

parts.note: re means on, concerning, as in a letter heading
a sting is a police operation to catch criminals

explanation.surface: An off-duty officer is placed on an undercover operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle, taking a break, or an actor between jobs: a synonym.

parts.note: the tennis star Chris Evert was briefly married to the golfer Greg Norman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer's former wife joins a sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' suggests a Norman conquest; it is Greg Norman, whose former wife is Chris Evert.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Liverpool football club.

clue.text: See wrong girl's top and behind

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see, as in 'lo and behold'
a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the next word, in this down clue

explanation.surface: Look at a misbehaving girl's top and her rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a rear end; here it is a match score.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailing on the scoreboard, as a team behind in a match is.

parts.note: a mission is a job or task

explanation.surface: Someone senses something missing in a former job.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing left out or absent, a gap.

clue.text: Season's spent with top Italian side

indicators.note: spent with top means the season loses its first letter, its top in this down clue

parts.note: winter is a season; the apostrophe s is no letter

explanation.surface: A season spent with a leading Italian football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Internazionale, usually called Inter Milan, is an Italian football club.

clue.text: This will be blown up reportedly — take cover

indicators.note: reportedly means it is said aloud, so the sound gives the answer

parts.note: a lilo is an inflatable mattress for the beach or pool, one that is blown up

explanation.surface: A warning that something is about to explode: get down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' suggests an explosion; it is a lilo, the British name for an inflatable airbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide or keep out of sight, staying quiet until danger passes.

indicators.note: part says the letters are a portion of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A performer's girlfriend is joining in the show.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer or creative practitioner, such as a singer or painter.

indicators.note: arrested means held, so the head word keeps the other piece inside it

parts.note: main means chief or head
ain't is a slang form of isn't

explanation.surface: A prisoner protests the chief has not been detained.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert or declare firmly: a synonym.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man he will end up with a particular woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mia is a woman's first name, so it can stand for any she.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
originally suggests the word was once arranged differently, signalling an anagram

parts.note: a germ is the beginning of something, as of an idea

explanation.surface: A sporting race that started in Athens, as the marathon did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' makes THEANS, which is opened up after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A people or nation, here Germany's footballers, viewed as a race.

indicators.note: almost says the synonym for dark falls short by its last letter

parts.note: night is the dark, as in 'after dark'

explanation.surface: Is it nearly dark? Very nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for near or nearly, as in 'the end is nigh'.
